description: The key set behind db/settings.json. Same kind of value as const.json holds, but changeable at runtime instead of at release. The tables are generic; this file is what makes a row typed, bounded and readable by both implementations.
valueEncoding: Every value in the database is text, in the same form contracts/ uses everywhere: a decimal string for every numeric type, 'true' or 'false' for bool, UTC milliseconds for an instant. 'default' below carries that same text form, so a default and a stored value are never encoded differently.

logging.level.description: The threshold below which a line is not emitted. The number is the contract, the spelling is not — see logging.json.
logging.level.note: Also needed before the database is open, so env carries a boot level and this key takes over once the settings table has been read. The two disagreeing during startup is expected and is not a bug.

auth.jwt_expires_seconds.description: Lifetime of a login token, and therefore how long after closing the tab a member stays signed in.
auth.jwt_expires_seconds.note: Legacy accepts either '10m' or a number of seconds. gradido2 takes seconds only: a duration grammar is a second parser to agree on, and the two implementations would agree on it approximately.

auth.redeem_jwt_expires_seconds.description: Lifetime of the token that carries a redeem across communities.

email.code_valid_minutes.description: How long a code sent by mail stays usable.

email.code_request_minutes.description: How long a member must wait before asking for a new code. Raising it is the lever against someone hammering the mail sender.

federation.validate_community_interval_m.description: How often known communities are re-validated.

dlt.active.description: Whether transactions are written to the distributed ledger.

dlt.connector_url.description: Base URL of the dlt-connector. Read when dlt.active is true.

gdt.active.description: Whether the GDT service is queried.

gdt.api_url.description: Base URL of the GDT API. Read when gdt.active is true.

gms.active.description: Whether the Geographic Member Search integration is offered.

gms.api_url.description: Base URL of the GMS API.

gms.dashboard_url.description: Where a member is sent to see the map.

gms.create_user_throw_errors.description: Whether a failure to create the member in GMS fails the registration, or is only logged. False means a GMS outage does not stop people signing up.

matching.active.description: Whether the matching feature — entries, map, list — is offered to members. Deliberately separate from gms.active: that one switches the older integration and is on in production, and hanging matching off it would publish unfinished work the moment an instance enables the old service.

humhub.active.description: Whether the HumHub based community server is connected.

humhub.api_url.description: Base URL of the HumHub API. NULL is the not-configured case and is only reachable while humhub.active is false — legacy declares no default for it either.

klicktipp.active.description: Whether members are subscribed to the Klicktipp newsletter service.

klicktipp.api_url.description: Base URL of the Klicktipp API. https only.
klicktipp.api_url.note: The credentials that go with it — user, password and the two API keys — are not settings. They travel together and they travel through the secret store.

crea.active.description: Whether the AI moderation assistant is available. One switch for the assistant and its chat window, so the two are never half on.
crea.active.note: The API key behind it is a secret and is not in this file.

crea.stub.description: Return a canned evaluation instead of calling the API, so the UI, the database path and the deterministic parts can be exercised without a key. An opt-in preview, off in production.

notes: A key is an identifier and follows the rule the rest of contracts/ follows: rename nothing, reuse nothing. To retire one, mark it deprecated and leave it here — a database written by an older release still holds rows under the old name.
'default' is what an implementation returns when no row exists, and every implementation returns exactly this. It is not a suggestion and it is not re-derived from an environment variable.

A default of null is only legal together with nullable: true. Everywhere else null in the database is a value that failed to parse, and the reading implementation falls back to this default and logs an error — see db/settings.json.

min, max and the string bounds are validation for the admin frontend and for both implementations, which must reject the same value. A bound is not decoration: auth.jwt_expires_seconds without a max is an admin-editable path to a token that never expires.

No secrets. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET, HUMHUB_JWT_KEY, GMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET, LOGIN_APP_SECRET, LOGIN_SERVER_KEY and the Klicktipp credentials stay in the OS secret store; see Architecture.md, Config. If a leak of the value is an incident, it is not a setting.

Deliberately not here, with the reason: COMMUNITY_NAME, COMMUNITY_URL, COMMUNITY_DESCRIPTION and COMMUNITY_LOCATION are columns on the home community row in db/communities.json; DECAY_START_TIME comes from shared-native and a copy here would be a second source of truth for a determinism-critical value (working rule 5); COMMUNITY_REDEEM_URL and every EMAIL_LINK_* are derived from the community URL and are constants in code; BACKEND_PORT, NODE_ENV, PRODUCTION, DEBUG, APP_VERSION, BUILD_COMMIT and the database connection are needed before the settings table can be read and stay in env; LOG4JS_CONFIG, LOG_FILES_BASE_PATH and USE_CRYPTO_WORKER are per-implementation infrastructure (working rule 4); GMS_USER_SEARCH_FRONTEND_ROUTE is frontend-only (working rule 3); GRAPHIQL has no meaning without GraphQL, which gradido2 does not have.

crea.model, crea.effort and crea.fast_mode are deliberately absent. They live in db/crea_settings.json today, and whether that singleton folds into the settings table is an open question recorded there and in db/settings.json. Writing them here before it is answered would create the second source of truth the question exists to avoid.
